headline: Showers taper off Sunday; a cool, mostly dry week ahead, with possible rain Saturday.
summary: A cold front has moved east of the Cascades, and a cool dip in the upper atmosphere is moving inland from the ocean, arriving Monday night. Leftover showers end Sunday, with some new snow in the higher mountains. Monday is a bit cooler with a few showers, and Tuesday should be dry, possibly with morning fog. A system passes south of the area Wednesday. After that, a blocked pattern, with high pressure to the north and a low to the south, keeps Western Washington dry from Wednesday night through Friday. Highs stay near 50 and lows drop into the 20s and 30s by Thursday. Saturday may bring rain, but forecasters are unsure how much.
